hook.text: ICON, a construction company, 3D-printed a hotel in Marfa, Texas—walls, curves.

buildup.text: 3D printing uses concrete or composite materials extruded through a nozzle. It can create organic.

discovery.text: A 3D-printed structure can be completed in days rather than months. Labor costs drop dramatically—the printer doesn't rest.

twist.text: The technology is still limited: multi-story buildings are tough, and printed structures still need conventional interiors.

climax.text: 3D printing could enable unique, sculptural hotels in remote locations where traditional construction is prohibitively expensive.

punchline.text: Layer by layer, a hotel appears. 3D printing makes impossible shapes buildable.

quiz.question: What is a current limitation of 3D-printed buildings?
options: Multi-story structures are challenging and conventional roofing is still needed
